hook.line: SEO and answer engine optimisation are complicated; there are no quick easy wins.
hook.visual: Head-on face cam, purple lights; a tilted yellow-on-black 'DODGY SEO SERVICES' sticker for one frame, then a white card 'BE CAREFUL OF DODGY SEO SERVICES' fills the lower half

beats.what: Opening frame: yellow 'DODGY SEO SERVICES' title slapped diagonally over the presenter
Cut to the white 'BE CAREFUL' card in the lower half, kept on screen while he states the problem
Card swaps to a screenshot of the Facebook ad he is calling out (before/after analytics)
Zoom punch as he describes the 'before vs after using their software' screenshots
Second zoom punch on 'look at the results they're promising'; screenshot shows the 'After' traffic curve
Verdict line: calls the claims nonsense and fake, while the inflated graph stays visible
Explains the backlinks and daily posts are spam; caption word 'SPAM' over the graph
Returns to the 'BE CAREFUL OF DODGY SEO SERVICES' card for the closing warning
Ends on 'be careful out there' with the same card, no CTA

why_it_works: A named villain (a real ad screenshot) gives the rant proof, so the viewer watches the graph instead of just a talking head
The warning card bookends the video, so the takeaway is the first and last thing seen
Protective tone ('I want to warn you') builds trust and invites comments from people who were burned
weaknesses: One continuous shot for 71 s with only two zoom punches; little visual change in the long middle
Small screenshot text is unreadable on a phone (most text sits outside the safe area)
No call to action, so the trust built is not converted into a follow or comment prompt
for_robert: Hold up the bad example as a screenshot card under the face and let Fred react to it (side-eye, poke the fake graph) instead of only describing it.
